name: Hania Wojciechowski
role: Clothing and fashion vendor, specializing in bespoke identity garments and faction-adjacent style
location: The Burnished Market, Copperhead, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Hania Wojciechowski is slight, with deep golden-brown skin, sharp cheekbones, and hair that shifts color through the full visible spectrum across a thirty-minute cycle â€” a geneware expression mod they saved for two years to afford and consider the single best decision of their life. They dress in deliberate contradiction: they could wear anything in their inventory but typically choose a single elegant piece against something plainly utilitarian, the combination always pointing at something the observer can't quite name. Their stall is a canvas archway strung with hanging garments that act as walls â€” inside, bolts of smart-fabric, hand-stenciled jackets, deconstructed corporate uniforms resewn into something feral, faction colors assembled into outfits that signal affiliation without commitment.

Vala is an expert in the semiotics of dress in GLMZ â€” they can read who someone is, what they want to be, and what they're afraid of from what they're wearing and how they hold themselves in it. This makes them an extraordinary vendor and an occasionally unsettling conversationalist. They are warm but precise, never cruel, but they will tell you what your clothes say about you if you ask, and sometimes if you don't. They have a genuine investment in helping people look the way they feel inside, and they extend credit to people in the Burnished Market who are clearly trying to climb out of something.

core_fears: Being seen as frivolous â€” that what they make doesn't matter
That their ability to read people means no one can surprise them, and they'll die bored and alone
core_desires: To make someone feel like themselves for the first time
Recognition â€” not fame, but the specific acknowledgment that what they do is art
coping_mechanisms: Aesthetic problem-solving â€” when emotionally overwhelmed, they make something
Compartmentalizing feelings as 'not productive right now'
blind_spots: So good at constructing image that they sometimes mistake curated presentation for genuine connection
Underestimates physical danger because they navigate social danger so fluently
psychology.secret: They have been quietly, carefully constructing a complete wardrobe for a person who doesn't exist â€” a fictional identity, documented through clothing. They don't know if it's art, a plan, or something they haven't named yet.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Elegant and specific â€” precise textile and color terminology, Ghanaian-Bengali turns of phrase from their parents, occasional sharp slang when the elegance drops
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, with pauses that feel intentional, like they're choosing each word from a rack and checking the fit
verbal_tics: Tilts their head when assessing someone, silently, for just a beat too long
example_lines: 'You want the jacket that says you're not afraid. But what you're wearing says you're trying to convince yourself. Those are different garments.'
'I don't do corporate cosplay. I do people. What do you actually want to look like when you walk into a room?'

story_hooks: A client came to them wanting to look like a mid-level Tessera employee â€” convincingly, down to the ID-adjacent color codes. Vala made it. Now that client is missing and someone is asking questions.

The fictional wardrobe they've been building has started attracting attention â€” someone in the Burnished Market believes the 'person' it belongs to is real and has started leaving messages addressed to them
narrative_function: Disguise and identity resource, social information broker (knows who's wearing what faction colors and why), gateway to Copperhead gang-adjacent networks, personal stylist with a gift for reading people
augmentations: Full-spectrum color-shifting hair (geneware expression mod); no cyberware; fingertip haptic sensitivity mod (improves fabric evaluation)
daily_life: They spend mornings sourcing fabric at the early Burnished Market wholesale hour, afternoons selling and doing fittings in the stall, and late evenings doing alterations and new construction by a single lamp in the back.
affiliation: Independent; informal relationships with several Copperhead gang-adjacent collectives who commission 'looks' seasonally

decision_rules: Never make something that will get someone killed â€” if a commission feels like a trap or a target, decline
Always give people the honest read, not the comfortable one
escalation_ladder: Deliberately becoming unreadable â€” expression goes neutral, voice goes flat
Exiting the stall entirely and locking it; they do not fight

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Observant and welcoming, asks one good question and listens fully to the answer
interpersonal_modes.friends: Teasing, generous, sometimes startlingly vulnerable when the professionalism drops

stress_responses.low: Starts working with their hands while talking â€” pins, needles, adjustments
stress_responses.medium: Gets very still and very precise
stress_responses.high: Abandons conversation entirely and sews for hours without speaking

contradictions: Champions authenticity but is themselves a masterwork of constructed presentation
habits: Evaluates every person they meet as a potential garment problem to solve â€” what would make them look right?
Leaves a folded scrap of fabric on the market E.L.F. shrine each week
Can't walk past a fabric bolt without touching it
breaking_points: Someone destroying one of their pieces
Being dismissed as 'just a clothes vendor'

timeline.event: Born in Copperhead; Ghanaian-Bengali father, Bulgarian-Peruvian mother, both small-market vendors
Began apprenticing at a smart-fabric workshop in the Burnished Market at age 14
Saved enough to buy the stall space and open independently; got the hair mod the same month
First commissioned 'identity wardrobe' for a Copperhead collective â€” established faction-adjacent reputation
Began construction of the fictional identity wardrobe; reason unclear even to themselves

physical_description.heritage: Eastern European dominant (51.5%) with significant Sub-Saharan African (32.5%) and Indigenous American (16%) ancestry; a striking tri-continental blend creating warm golden-brown skin with pronounced cheekbone definition, rich facial fullness through the lower face, and refined bone structure characteristic of Eastern European ancestry combined with the warmth and depth of Sub-Saharan and Indigenous American genetic expression
physical_description.build: Slight and angular, with defined collarbones and long fingers; the build of someone who moves through crowded spaces easily and spends hours at a sewing table
physical_description.hair_color: Full-spectrum chromatic cycling (currently: deep violet fading to amber to cyan across a 30-minute loop)
physical_description.hair_style: Loose, shoulder-length waves with deliberate asymmetry; left side pinned back with a salvaged circuit board clasp
physical_description.eye_color: Deep warm brown with amber undertones
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-brown with rich undertones; the blended result of Eastern European base warmed and deepened by Sub-Saharan and Indigenous American ancestry, creating a complex intermediate tone with subtle golden luminosity
physical_description.complexion: Balanced intermediate featuresâ€”prominent defined cheekbones with warmth, moderate temples, fine-featured face with Sub-Saharan fullness and softness through the lower face and jawline; skin kept meticulously clean despite Market dust; minimal makeup, favoring bare lips and defined brows; nose bridge refined with subtle width typical of multi-heritage ancestry blending
distinguishing_marks: Faint white scarring across inner left wrist (old self-harm history, now healed)
Thin, precise line tattoo running down the right collarbone in an abstract textile pattern (geometric weaving symbol)
Small burn mark on left thumb pad (fabric-work accident, now faded to pale pink)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Hair geneware mod (chromatic cycling) is immediately striking and intentional. Fingertip haptic sensitivity mod shows only as slightly higher skin sensitivity around fingertipsâ€”not visually obvious. No visible cyberware.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision; stands with weight balanced evenly, ready to shift. Hands are often in motionâ€”gesturing, arranging fabric, touching materials to evaluate texture. Eye contact is direct and assessing without being hostile. They have a habit of tilting their head slightly when evaluating someone's outfit.
physical_description.clothing_style: Deliberate contradiction is their uniform: today might be a pristine white linen shirt (corporate salvage, refitted) paired with cargo pants patched in mismatched smart-fabric samples. Tomorrow: a hand-stenciled denim jacket over a plain grey undershirt and tailored black trousers. Footwear is always practical (worn canvas boots or reinforced street shoes). Accessories include salvaged tech components repurposed as jewelryâ€”circuit board clasps, LED pendant, fabric scraps tied as wrist wraps. Everything is meticulously maintained despite the Market grime. Tier 4 aesthetic with Tier 3 resourcefulness and Tier 2 design sensibility.
